subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be categorically denied `sessions.patch` access to legacy ownerless session rows after upgrade?
rationale: Exact owner equality is a defensible fail-closed rule for foreign rows, but ownerless rows predate the ownership contract and the proposed behavior intentionally breaks their existing plugin-runtime access.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Require an exact persisted `pluginOwnerId` match for every plugin-runtime patch, accepting the legacy upgrade break.

options.title: Migrate ownership first
options.body: Add a dedicated, auditable migration that establishes safe ownership before enforcing exact equality.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Require an exact persisted `pluginOwnerId` match for every plugin-runtime patch, accepting the legacy upgrade break.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged session-ownership work and original `sessions.patch` feature history make this the strongest available owner for the boundary decision.
